solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aussie weed patch with wild spurges less acceptable

indicators.note: wild things run out of control, so the letters break out of their printed order
'less' means minus, so something is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: to cobble is to patch or mend roughly
taken as written
U means socially acceptable, upper-class usage; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a weedy patch overrun with spurges is a less pleasing sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less acceptable' reads as a comparison, but it splits: 'less' removes the letter for 'acceptable', from the old British U (upper-class) versus non-U speech distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbler's pegs is an Australian name for the weed Bidens pilosa, whose barbed seeds stick to clothing.

clue.text: See red coucal wandering about some trees

indicators.note: something wandering strays from its set course, so these letters drift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is told to spot a red coucal, a cuckoo-like bird, roaming around in the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is part of the definition, not a container signal: the answer is an adjective meaning relating to certain trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedrelaceous describes plants of the cedar-wood family of tropical timber trees, so it concerns a particular group of them.

clue.text: Mouthlike aperture very large on tailless mosquito

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
Culex is the genus of common mosquitoes; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes a mouth-shaped opening on a huge mosquito that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The mosquito is its Latin genus name, a Mephisto-level piece of knowledge. In a down clue 'on' means the second piece sits below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An oscule is a small mouth-like opening, such as the outflow pore through which a sponge expels water.

clue.text: Sad fool climbing tree

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool

explanation.surface: A sorry idiot is up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUE plus MUG reversed. 'Mug' for a fool is common British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue gum is a species of eucalyptus, a tall Australian tree with bluish bark and leaves.

clue.text: The French outing was uncontrolled

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: A French excursion got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of the phrase is the same as its present, so 'was uncontrolled' fits it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is to act or speak without restraint, giving full vent to feeling or energy.

clue.text: Dialect wrongly used in an official order

indicators.note: something done wrongly is not in its proper form, so the letters are set in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A regional way of speaking has been misused in a formal decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in an official order' is the whole definition, an adjectival phrase, not a further instruction to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Edictal is the adjective from edict, a proclamation by an authority, so it describes what pertains to such a decree.

clue.text: Free acknowledgment holds nothing for one

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means X stands in the place of Y, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a salute is a gesture of acknowledgment
O looks like zero, nothing
A means one, as in 'a book'; this letter is replaced

explanation.surface: A free acknowledgment is worth nothing to anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: SALUTE with its A changed to O. The definition is a rare botanical sense of the word as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany solute means loose or not adhering, so it can stand for free in the sense of unattached.

clue.text: Local swell — prince with a lot of capital

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so one letter is dropped from the end

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
Lima is the capital of Peru; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A local toff, a prince, owns a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like a noun for a dandy, and 'capital' like money; it is a verb and a city. 'Local' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plim is a dialect verb meaning to fill out or puff up, a regional equivalent of the verb to swell.

clue.text: Instrument, small, introduced to upper throat

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put inside it

parts.note: gula is the anatomical term for the upper part of the throat, the gullet
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A little instrument, perhaps a tube, is inserted into someone's upper throat.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside GULA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gusla is a one-stringed bowed folk fiddle played in the Balkans to accompany epic songs.

clue.text: Spot old jelly — see in cooked pig, perhaps

parts.note: spie is an archaic spelling of spy, to spot

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: a gel is a jelly-like substance
taken as written: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cook spots some old jelly inside a roast pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' is not the animal: pig iron is crude iron cast in moulds. 'Old' tells you the spelling of the first piece is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiegeleisen is a manganese-rich pig iron used in steelmaking, so it is one example of pig iron.

clue.text: Returned some caramelised old vinegar

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the letters read right to left
'some' means only part of what follows, so the letters sit inside a longer word

parts.note: five consecutive letters near the end of the word

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a dish of caramelised food made with an aged vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside caramELISEd and is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Esile is an obsolete word for vinegar, found in Spenser and Shakespeare, hence 'old'.

clue.text: Shout to horse carrying veteran highwayman

definitions.note: strictly a robbery; the answer stands for the man who commits it

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hup is a call to a horse to go on or turn
a veteran is old

explanation.surface: A cry to a horse bearing an ageing highwayman.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene of horse and highwayman is all of a piece, which hides where the definition starts; the answer names the crime standing in for its perpetrator.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is an armed robbery on the road, the very trade of a mounted robber of travellers.

clue.text: Capital dress for fishing above waterfall

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed above another comes before it

parts.note: to dub a fly is to dress it, tying on feathers for angling
lin, or linn, is a Scots word for a waterfall

explanation.surface: Smart clothing for a fishing trip above a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital dress' reads as excellent clothing, but 'Capital' is the definition alone. Linn is a Scots word, as in place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital city of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Calico utilises partly cotton material

indicators.note: 'partly' means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A calico fabric is said to be made partly of cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across calICO UTILises. Calico is itself a cotton cloth, which makes it look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coutil is a closely woven cotton twill used for corsets and mattress covers.

clue.text: Regret about Liberal government

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to rue is to regret
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Remorse over a Liberal administration.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule is the exercise of authority over a state, the same as governing or government.

clue.text: Cold roll which may be served for pudding

definitions.text: which may be served for pudding
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a rumble is a roll, as of thunder or drums

explanation.surface: A cold bread roll that might be offered as dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' suggests bread; it is the deep rolling sound. Pudding is the British word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumble is a baked dessert of stewed fruit topped with a crumbly mix of flour, butter and sugar.

clue.text: Run away after European writ of execution

indicators.note: a piece placed after another follows it in the answer

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
to leg it is slang for running away

explanation.surface: Someone flees after a European court issues an order against them.
explanation.walkthrough: E comes first, with LEG IT after it. 'Leg it' is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegit was a legal writ allowing a creditor to take possession of a debtor's goods or land until paid.

clue.text: Prison camp for males outside Los Angeles

indicators.note: one piece sitting outside another wraps round it

parts.note: a stag event, such as a stag party, is for men only
LA is the abbreviation for Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A men's prison camp just beyond Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for males' is a single piece: a stag night is a British bachelor party, so stag means men only.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War, especially one for enlisted men.

clue.text: Poor labourer — key contributor to immature movement

parts.note: a prole is a working-class person, a proletarian
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: An impoverished worker plays a key role in a juvenile political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Immature movement' looks like a naive political cause; it is a larva crawling, and the answer is one of the limbs it walks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A proleg is a fleshy stumpy limb on the abdomen of a caterpillar, helping the larva get about.

clue.text: Like a dirndl incorporating eastern fabric

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the dirndl is the traditional dress of the Alpine regions
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A Tyrolean-style dress made with some cloth from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside ALPINE. A dirndl is the full-skirted dress of Bavaria and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Alepine is a mixed fabric of wool and silk or cotton, a kind of woven cloth.

clue.text: Eagle, say, in the place cited eating eastern seabird

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: LC is short for loco citato, Latin for 'in the place cited'
E is the abbreviation for eastern
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An eagle, for example, is recorded here devouring a seabird from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eagle' looks like a bird beside the seabird, but church reading desks are often carved as eagles. 'in the place cited' is a Latin reference abbreviation used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Many church lecterns are shaped as an eagle with outspread wings supporting the Bible, so an eagle is an example.

clue.text: Cushy for a thespian's pad

parts.note: a plum job is a cushy one
per means for each, for a, as in 'per day'

explanation.surface: An easy number: an actor's comfortable flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' reads as a flat; it is padding. 'for a' is not link words but a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumper is a pad worn inside the mouth to fill out the cheeks, used by actors changing their appearance.

clue.text: Losing pressure, flying Imperial planes cover this quickly

indicators.note: things flying are scattered through the air, so the letters land in a new order
losing something means going without it, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure; this letter is removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Aircraft of an Imperial air force, flying low after cabin pressure fails, cover distance fast.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPERIAL without P is rearranged. The definition is the whole closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An air mile is a unit of distance flown, a nautical mile measured in flight, which aircraft travel in seconds.

clue.text: Mental image I had over Scots headgear

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of 'I had'
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
in Scots a lum hat, or lum, is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone recalls picturing themselves in a Scottish hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as a position word, but it is a piece; in cricket an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolum is a phantom or mental picture, an idea formed in the mind; the word is Latin for apparition.

clue.text: Striking after digging stick being found in mine?

indicators.note: a piece that comes after another follows it in the answer

parts.note: a ko is a Maori digging stick
bold means striking, eye-catching

explanation.surface: A miner strikes after the digging stick turns up underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' looks like a verb but is a noun, a creature; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A kobold is a goblin of German folklore said to haunt mines, so it is a spirit creature living underground.

clue.text: See Strictly's setting up a dance number

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for 'see'

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up turns it to read upward, so its letters go backwards

parts.note: Strictly Come Dancing is a TV show, so it is tele
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch the TV dance show stage a new routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strictly' is Strictly Come Dancing, a British TV ballroom contest, standing for TV, not the adverb. 'number' belongs to the definition, as in a musical number.
explanation.definitionFit: The veleta is an old-time round dance in waltz time, popular in British ballrooms.

clue.text: Earthy disgust about department director

indicators.note: 'about' means round, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to cloy is to sicken or disgust with excess
D is the abbreviation for department
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: Crude revulsion directed at a head of department.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOY goes round two Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloddy means full of clods, lumps of earth, so it describes soil that is earthy and lumpy.

clue.text: Lake near strange swamp

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lake lies close to an eerie marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' reads as a position word but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerna is the marshy region in Greece where Hercules killed the Hydra, and the name came to mean a marsh or bog.

clue.text: Lava flow could cut ends off esplanade

indicators.note: a cut word is shortened, its final letter trimmed away

parts.note: taken as written; its last letter goes

indicators.note: the ends off a word are its first and last letters, taken from it

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A stream of molten rock might sever both ends of a seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' and 'ends off' look like one instruction on the esplanade; really 'could' is cut, and the ends are taken off the esplanade.
explanation.definitionFit: A coulee is a stream of molten or solidified lava, from the French word for flowing.

clue.text: East give assistance after Hungary's exported fish

indicators.note: a piece that comes after another follows it in the answer

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

indicators.note: something exported is sent out of the country, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to help out is to give assistance
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Eastern Europe sends aid after Hungary's fish exports.
explanation.walkthrough: E is followed by HELP OUT minus H. The possessive on Hungary is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The eelpout is an eel-like marine fish, also called a viviparous blenny, and the name is used for the burbot too.

clue.text: African currency bond abandoned by company

indicators.note: what is abandoned by someone is left without them, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: a copula is a link or bond, as in grammar
CO is the abbreviation for company; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: An African money bond is dropped by a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: COPULA loses CO from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: The pula is the monetary unit of Botswana, named after the Setswana word for rain.

clue.text: Indian employer sacking last local gardener

indicators.note: sacking the last one means dismissing the final member, so the end letter goes

parts.note: malik is an Indian word for a master or employer

explanation.surface: An Indian boss fires the latest gardener he hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' means Indian here, picked up from the wordplay's setting; it is not the gardener next door.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a mali is a man employed to tend a garden, the local term for a hired garden worker.

clue.text: The Spanish poet goes back to positive subjects

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for positive

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
Edgar Allan Poe, the American poet

explanation.surface: A Spanish poet returns to upbeat themes.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is American, not Spanish; 'The Spanish' is its own piece. 'subjects' reads as topics, but it means citizens under a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's subjects are the people of the realm, the population under that ruler's authority.

clue.text: Separate university in blunder losing billions

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
losing something means going without it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a bungle is a blunder
B is the abbreviation for billions; this letter is removed
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university splits off after a costly mistake that wasted billions.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNGLE loses B, then U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unglue is to detach things stuck together, so it is a verb meaning to part or disconnect them.

clue.text: Abandoned English picked up in Spenser

parts.note: something abandoned is left
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A forsaken English work is rediscovered in Spenser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up in Spenser' tells you the answer is a Spenserian form; it is not a pick-up-the-sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used lefte as the past tense of lift, so in The Faerie Queene it means raised or lifted.

clue.text: Surviving fire alone, artist gets academy to replace oxygen everywhere

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so one letter is swapped in for another
everywhere means in every position, so the swap is made at each occurrence, not only once

parts.note: solo means alone
Piet Mondrian, the Dutch abstract painter
A is the abbreviation for academy
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen; every one is replaced

explanation.surface: An artist who survived a fire alone is welcomed into an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLO MONDRIAN with every O changed to A. 'everywhere' means all three Os are swapped, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: The salamander was fabled to live unharmed in flames, so salamandrian describes anything that endures fire.
